samples.question: This image has two horizontal rails, an upper one and a lower one. Both rails are the same track: the five short black ticks on the upper rail are five landmarks of that track, the five short black ticks on the lower rail are the same five landmarks in the same left-to-right order, and each thin grey line joins a landmark on the upper rail to the same landmark on the lower rail. Between two neighbouring landmarks the lower rail is a uniformly stretched or squeezed copy of the upper rail, so a point that sits a given fraction of the way from one landmark to the next on the upper rail sits at that same fraction of the way between the two matching landmarks on the lower rail. The stretch factor is different on different stretches of rail, so no single shift or single scale carries positions across, and the distance from a landmark in pixels carries no information across. The black triangle above the upper rail marks one point of the upper rail, at the tip of the triangle. Four coloured dots hang below the lower rail, each on a short stem that meets the lower rail at that dot's position. Exactly one of those dots stands at the point of the lower rail that matches the point marked by the triangle. Which dot is it? Answer with that dot's colour: blue, brown, green, orange, purple, or red.
